evals.prompt: I want a commitment curve for a study called smoke_commitment. My design inputs are in ./data/smoke_inputs, parents should go to ./runs/smoke_parents, runs under ./runs, and I want to track the design metrics only (no refolding). Grid every 15 steps. Build me the configs.
evals.expected_output: A smoke_commitment study spec and three generated YAML configs at configs/inference_experiment/smoke_commitment_phase1.yaml, configs/inference_experiment/smoke_commitment_sweep.yaml, and configs/sweeps/smoke_commitment.yaml, with matching design metric tags, phase-2 num_replicates: 1, and a partial_trajectory_fraction_steps grid of 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0.

requires: rfd4-proteina-setup complete; no GPU needed for config generation

assertions: Writes a spec YAML with name/inputs/parents_dir/out_root, metrics_tags: [design], and phase2.step: 15
Runs open-models-skills/rfd4-proteina/rfd4-proteina-commitment-curves/scripts/make_configs.py --spec <spec>
Produces configs/inference_experiment/smoke_commitment_{phase1,sweep}.yaml and configs/sweeps/smoke_commitment.yaml
The phase-2 config sets num_replicates: 1 and adds no sampling_transforms block
The two experiment configs declare the same metrics_tags
The sweep grid holds 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0 for step 15 of 60

evals.prompt: Set up a commitment curve over the 4 designs I have in ./runs/tiny. Grid every 5 steps.
evals.expected_output: An explanation that four parents leave a very wide correlation confidence interval, recommending at least 40 parents through phase-1 replication without increasing phase-2 children as a substitute.

requires: a directory holding 4 design CIFs; no GPU needed

assertions: Points out that rho is computed across parents, so 4 parents give a confidence interval near +/-0.9
Recommends 40+ parents, and generating replicates in phase 1 rather than children in phase 2
Does not silently raise phase-2 num_replicates to compensate

evals.prompt: Here are the metrics from my phase-1 parents: ./runs/smoke_phase1/per_example_metrics.csv. Before I pay for the sweep, show me how rare each of the metrics I care about actually is.
evals.expected_output: A metric_distributions.csv and at least two light/dark metric_distributions PNGs under ./runs/smoke_phase1/analysis, with configured pass thresholds and per-cut 1-in-N rates clearly distinguishing measured counts from unreliable or extrapolated estimates.

requires: a per_example_metrics.csv holding at least one column named by a pass criterion

assertions: Runs open-models-skills/rfd4-proteina/rfd4-proteina-commitment-curves/scripts/metric_distributions.py with --metrics_csv and --out_dir, not commitment_curve.py
Lets the thresholds come from the pass-criteria config rather than hand-typing them, and points --pass_criteria at the run's own config if it used a custom metrics group
Writes metric_distributions.csv plus light and dark PNGs: one histogram per metric, pass-criteria thresholds as vertical cuts
Reports the pass rate per cut as '1 in N designs', and for a cut fewer than 10 designs passed names the extrapolation it quoted (GPD tail or the density family) rather than presenting it as measured
Flags a bimodal metric whose density fit is marked 'poor fit', or a cut whose two estimates disagree by 10x, as not resolvable rather than quoting the number
Does not claim a criterion is impossible when the caption reads 'ends before the cut'

evals.prompt: I already have a finished sweep. Plot the commitment curve for one metric from ./runs/smoke_sweep/sweep_per_example_metrics.csv against the parents in ./runs/smoke_phase1/per_example_metrics.csv.
evals.expected_output: Commitment and fidelity CSVs plus light/dark curve PNGs under ./runs/smoke_sweep/analysis, with interpretation of the between-problem floor, reproducibility ceiling, and clean-end fidelity checks.

requires: a sweep master CSV with generation.args.partial_trajectory_fraction_steps and task columns
a phase-1 parent CSV whose example_id values match those tasks

assertions: Runs open-models-skills/rfd4-proteina/rfd4-proteina-commitment-curves/scripts/commitment_curve.py with --sweep_csv, --parent_csv, --out_dir and a --metrics 'Label=column' spec
Writes commitment_curve.csv plus light and dark PNGs under the out_dir
Also writes fidelity_curve.csv and its PNGs without being asked, and does not spend a --metrics slot on sequence identity or CA RMSD
Reports the step-0 value as a between-problem floor rather than calling it zero memory
Reports the value at the highest restart step as the metric's own reproducibility ceiling if it is below 1
Checks the clean end on the fidelity curves (identity ~100%, CA RMSD ~0 A) before interpreting rho
